Switches, Miscellaneous Requestor: Julius Heslop SINGLE PHASE ELECTRONIC RECLOSER, RATED FOR 15KV AND 400A OF CONTINOUS CURRENT. CAPABLE OF INTERRUPTING FAULTS UP TO 8KA. RATED FOR 30,000 MECHANICAL OPERATIONS. WEIGHT OF THE UNIT SHALL BE 55 LBS OR LESS, AND A LIGHTING IMPULSE WITHSTAND OF 125KV. THE RECLOSER INTERUPTER, DRIVE MECHANISM, CONTROL, AND HOUSING SHALL BE AT SYSTEM POTENTIAL. RECLOSER SHALL BE SELF POWERED AND DESIGNED TO FUNCTION WITHOUT THE USE OF AN EXTERNAL TRANSFORMER FOR POWER. THE RECLOSER UNIT SHALL HAVE A MICROPROCESSOR BASED CONTROL WHICH SHALL ALLOW THE USER TO PROGRAM ANY OF THE 11 STANDARD RECLOSER CURVES. CONTROL SHALL ALSO ALLOW TO USER TO PROGRAM MINIMUM TRIP AND RESPONSE TIMES, NUMBER OF OPERATIONS TO LOCKOUT, AND COLD LOAD TIME. RECLOSER CONTROL SHALL STORE EVENT HISTORY FROM THE LAST 40 OVERCURRENT OPERATIONS AND SHALL ALSO HAVE A SCRATCH PAD NON-VOLTATILE MEMORY FOR USER ENTERED NOTES. RECLOSER UNIT SHALL UTILIZE ENHANCED SECURITY PROTOCOL AND SUPPORT SIFLECT HIGH PERFORMANCE RADIO. THE RECLOSER CONROL SHALL BE INTERNAL TO THE RECLOSER HOUSING AND SHALL BE ACCESSIBLE VIA RADIO. ALL SETTINGS SHALL BE CAPABLE OF BEING SET VIA RADIO. THE RECLOSER UNIT SHALL HAVE A MANUAL YELLOW OPERATING HANDLE THAT MIMICS TRADITIONAL OCR RECLOSERS. THE RECLOSER UNIT SHALL ALSO HAVE AN AMBER LED LOCKOUT BEACON WHICH FLASHED FOR 4 HOURS. SHALL BE IN ACCORDANCE WITH LATEST REVISION OF E-1765

The tester shall be capable of outputting a continuously adjustable amperage of up to 3 amp from the front panel of the tester. A digital current meter shall be available on the control to display the current that is being applied. A connection for an external current meter for the purpose of calibrating the internal digital current meter shall also be integrated into the tester. A digital timer display shall also be available on the control for the purpose of timing open/close sequences of the recloser control, which will trigger the timer to start and stop. The tester shall be compatible with 14 pin style connectors used for Cooper recloser controls (compatible with Cooper Form 2, 3, 3A, 4A, 4C, 5, 6; and Type FX, FXA, FXB controls). A recloser simulator circuit shall be built into the tester to simulate recloser operation (indicated by red and green lights on the tester panel) and to simulate the response time of the recloser mechanism to trip and close signals. The tester shall have the ability to check operating sequence, control response time (phase and ground trip), reclosing time, and minimum trip current (for phase and ground). The tester shall be a self contained unit packaged in a weatherproof sturdy carrying case with a detachable front cover. The carrying case shall have provisions for storing the power cord, interconnecting cables, and spare fuses and bulbs. A three wire power cord with ground power plug shall also be provided. The tester shall weigh no more than 35 lbs and be no larger than 10 inches X 22 inches X 15 inches.

Application Software, Microcomputer Last year alone, the Fire/Arson section applied for (and was granted) over 20 criminal search warrants to look at cell phone data for active cases. We could have applied for more, but because we currently manually enter all of the lines of data from the CDR (call detail records), we do not order the number of CDRs that we should be ordering. Additionally, the ones that we do order, because of the manual entry, we usually only order 4 days worth of data. The fault in this is that we miss out on months of data that could be used to show movement patterns that suspects exhibit. A typical CDR has over 8 thousand lines of data - manually, that takes upwards of a full day to input AND interpret. The Cell Hawk software (used and recommended by the Travis County DA, APD's Homicide and Robbery unit, and the Travis County Fire Marshal) can analyze up to 100K CDRs in less than 4 minutes. I have been using the free demo version for one of our cases that involves 4 separate CDR's. In less than 30 minutes, I was able to plot all of the information and show cell phone movement that will be used to charge at least 3 suspects with Arson.

Application Software, Microcomputer Last year alone, the Fire/Arson section applied for (and was granted) over 20 criminal search warrants to look at cell phone data for active cases. We could have applied for more, but because we currently manually enter all of the lines of data from the CDR (call detail records), we do not order the number of CDRs that we should be ordering. Additionally, the ones that we do order, because of the manual entry, we usually only order 4 days worth of data. The fault in this is that we miss out on months of data that could be used to show movement patterns that suspects exhibit. A typical CDR has over 8 thousand lines of data - manually, that takes upwards of a full day to input AND interpret. The Cell Hawk software (used and recommended by the Travis County DA, APD's Homicide and Robbery unit, and the Travis County Fire Marshal) can analyze up to 100K CDRs in less than 4 minutes. I have been using the free demo version for one of our cases that involves 4 separate CDR's. In less than 30 minutes, I was able to plot all of the information and show cell phone movement that will be used to charge at least 3 suspects with Arson.

RELAYS, ELECTRONIC RFQ APC0559 The bidder shall supply an electronic recloser control tester. The tester shall be capable of outputting a continuously adjustable amperage of up to 3 amp from the front panel of the tester. A digital current meter shall be available on the control to display the current that is being applied. A connection for an external current meter for the purpose of calibrating the internal digital current meter shall also be integrated into the tester. A digital timer display shall also be available on the control for the purpose of timing open/close sequences of the recloser control, which will trigger the timer to start and stop. The tester shall be compatible with 14 pin style connectors used for Cooper recloser controls (compatible with Cooper Form 2, 3, 3A, 4A, 4C, 5, 6; and Type FX, FXA, FXB controls). A recloser simulator circuit shall be built into the tester to simulate recloser operation (indicated by red and green lights on the tester panel) and to simulate the response time of the recloser mechanism to trip and close signals. The tester shall have the ability to check operating sequence, control response time (phase and ground trip), reclosing time, and minimum trip current (for phase and ground). The tester shall be a self contained unit packaged in a weatherproof sturdy carrying case with a detachable front cover. The carrying case shall have provisions for storing the power cord, interconnecting cables, and spare fuses and bulbs. A three wire power cord with ground power plug shall also be provided. The tester shall weigh no more than 35 lbs and be no larger than 10 inches X 22 inches X 15 inches.
